title: Use consistent units
summary: Before comparing measurements, put them in the same units. Metres and centimetres describe length on different scales.
introduction: Before comparing measurements, put them in the same units. Metres and centimetres describe length on different scales. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Before comparing measurements, put them in the same units. Metres and centimetres describe length on different scales.

blocks.code:
lengths_cm = [100, 150, 200]
lengths_m = [value / 100 for value in lengths_cm]
print(lengths_m)
blocks.title: Use consistent units

blocks.text: The output is [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]. Each centimetre value is divided by 100 because a metre contains 100 centimetres.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Adding 1 metre and 50 centimetres as if they were both the same unit gives a wrong result.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).
